title: M3C2 Level of Detection (95% Confidence)

σ₁, σ₂.description: Local surface roughness (std dev) in epoch 1 and 2

n₁, n₂.description: Number of points in projection cylinder for each epoch

applicability: Spatially variable — LoD is different at every point. Rough surfaces and sparse areas have higher LoD. Typical LoD for TLS monitoring: 3–15 mm. Improvements: better registration (more targets), higher point density, smoother surfaces.

title: Displacement Vector from Multi-Epoch Point Tracking
applicability: For tracked discrete points (targets, natural features, or averaged surface patches). Magnitude: |d| = √(Δx²+Δy²+Δz²). Direction: azimuth and plunge of displacement vector. Decompose into horizontal and vertical components for interpretation.

title: Tilt from Differential Displacement
applicability: Fit plane to deformed surface; tilt = deviation from original orientation. For small angles: θ ≈ Δd/L (in radians). Alert thresholds vary by structure: retaining walls 0.5–1°, buildings 1/500 angular distortion.

title: Displacement Rate (Velocity)
applicability: Average velocity between epochs. For acceleration detection: a = (v₂ - v₁)/Δt. Inverse velocity (1/v vs. time) used for slope failure prediction (Fukuzono method): linear trend of 1/v → 0 predicts failure time.

title: Thermal Expansion Correction

Δd_thermal.description: Apparent displacement due to thermal expansion

applicability: Steel: α = 12×10⁻⁶/°C. Concrete: α = 10–12×10⁻⁶/°C. Rock: α = 5–10×10⁻⁶/°C. For a 50m dam face with ΔT = 20°C: Δd = 10–12 mm. Must correct or survey at consistent temperatures for mm-level monitoring.

title: Registration Error from Target Residuals

d_target_i.description: Residual at each target after registration

applicability: Computed from target residuals in cloud alignment. Should be < desired LoD. If σ_reg = 3 mm, theoretical LoD ≈ 6 mm minimum (even with perfect point cloud quality). Use stable check targets (not used in registration) to independently verify.

title: Tunnel Convergence from Cross-Section
equation: ΔD = D_T0 - D_Tn;  strain = ΔD / D_T0
applicability: Extract cross-sections at regular chainage (every 1–5 m). Compare diameters in multiple directions (horizontal, vertical, diagonals). Full profile comparison shows non-uniform convergence patterns indicating asymmetric loading.

title: Spatial Averaging for Improved Precision

n.description: Number of independent points in averaging area

applicability: Averaging displacement over a patch of n independent points improves precision by √n. 100 points → 10× improvement. Limited by spatial correlation — nearby points are not fully independent. Effective n may be less than total count.
